# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

This plan defines the process characterization studies for the ultrafiltration and diafiltration (UF/DF) step of the A-Mab drug substance process. UF/DF is Step `{python} STEP` and the last step of the drug substance train. It concentrates the antibody, exchanges the process buffer for the formulation buffer, and delivers the drug substance at its target concentration of `{python} g(sp(pconc))` g/L. The commercial process runs at a production bioreactor working volume of `{python} SCALE_L` L. The process is being transferred from the development site in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION` to the commercial drug substance site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`. The studies of this plan form part of the Stage 1 process design record that supports the transfer and the Biologics License Application (BLA) [@fda2011; @ichq10].

The plan covers the `{python} w(n_par)` process parameters of the step (@sec-factors), the scale-down model on which they are studied, the analytical methods and the sampling, the acceptance and decision criteria, and the analysis by which a proven acceptable range (PAR) is assigned to each parameter. It applies to the drug substance process only. Drug product manufacture and the development of the formulation belong to the drug product program and are out of scope. That program fixes the composition of the formulation buffer, and the studies treat it as a constant.

The step does not change the glycan variants of A-Mab, and no clearance of host cell protein, DNA or leached Protein A is credited to it (@sec-cqa). It can add to aggregate and to the acidic charge variants (@sec-uo). No viral clearance is claimed for this step.

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on `{python} V1_APPR`, before the first study of the step began on `{python} FIRST_START`. Version 2.0 is issued under the QA investigation INV-001, which QA opened on `{python} INV["opened"]` after its review of PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for BLA readiness, and closed on `{python} INV["closed"]`. The investigation found that the criteria used to judge each step in the PAR analysis had been set after the data were seen, and that no approved plan contained them (INV-001 finding 1). As corrective actions, PCMP-001 was reissued as Version 2.0 with acceptance criteria derived a priori (INV-001 action CA1), and the step plans were amended with those criteria and with the method for fragments (action CA2). This document is the amendment of PCP-010 under action CA2, and it is issued after the studies it governs were run. The design, the ranges, the levels and the sampling of Version 1.0 are unchanged, and so are its decision rules except where the list below says otherwise. Descriptions of the process that Version 1.0 stated wrongly are corrected without a change to the design (@sec-uo, @sec-sdm, @sec-stats). The changes are the following.

1. The acceptance criteria are stated on the basis of PCMP-001 Version 2.0. PCMP-001 §7.3 defines `{python} N_IAC` intermediate acceptance criteria (IACs) at `{python} w(N_IAC_STEPS)` steps, for the step outputs on which a drug substance criterion depends. Each carries the drug substance criterion back through the platform worst case of every downstream step. The platform worst case of a step is the lowest clearance, or the largest increase, that the step showed for the earlier antibodies X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. No step follows this one, so PCMP-001 defines no IAC for it, and the final retentate is judged against the drug substance criteria (@sec-crit-pq). Version 1.0 of this plan stated the same criteria. At analysis, however, Version 1.0 read the acidic charge variants against their upper limit of `{python} V1_AV_HI` % alone (INV-001 finding 4, a two-sided range assessed against its upper end). This plan keeps the two-sided criterion, and PCR-010 records the departure.
2. The scale-down model is qualified by its offset from manufacturing scale, as PCMP-001 §7.1 requires for every scale-down model (@sec-sdm). This replaces the qualification rule of Version 1.0, a test of equivalence in three parts (@sec-crit-sdm). PCMP-001 requires the qualification runs, and the estimate of each offset, before the first characterization run of a step. Under PCMP-001 the decision whether the model is qualified for an output is then made at analysis, on the response-surface model of the step. This step has none, so this plan sets no rule for that decision.
3. The statistics on which each output is judged are stated. Under PCMP-001 §6.2 a quality attribute is judged on a single batch, and a model term is significant at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`. Version 1.0 judges each run on its own measured result, which is a single batch (@sec-rules), and tests each slope at the same level (@sec-stats). The model-adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 and the verification of platform worst cases in PCMP-001 §7.5 work on response-surface models, so they do not apply at this step.
4. The analytical method decision AMD-001 of `{python} AMD["date"]` sets non-reduced CE-SDS (nrCE-SDS) as the method for fragments in every study at every step (PCMP-001 §7.8). Fragments are not an attribute of the studies of this step (@tbl-sampling), and @sec-cqa gives the reason.
5. The execution window of each study and the calibration status of the skid it used are stated (@sec-schedule). This answers INV-001 finding 5, that the Version 1.0 records gave no execution dates and the equipment tables therefore appeared to cite expired calibrations. The title block of Version 1.0 carried `{python} REV1["effective"]`, the date on which the Version 1.0 reports were approved, in place of the approval date of this plan. The revision history now gives the approval date.
6. The classification follows PCMP-001 §6.2 and §7.7 (@sec-class). Under §6.2 a parameter affects an attribute when its slope is significant at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`. Under §7.7 a significant effect that is too small to move the attribute appreciably within the PAR does not by itself make a parameter critical, and a parameter is well-controlled critical when its risk of falling outside its acceptable range is low. Version 1.0 classified every parameter whose variation affects a quality attribute as critical, or as well controlled critical where the risk of falling outside the design space is low. A parameter with a significant but small effect can therefore be classified as a key process parameter under Version 2.0, where Version 1.0 would have classified it as critical or well controlled critical.

This amendment describes only the studies that Version 1.0 planned. Work that Version 1.0 did not foresee is recorded in PCR-010 as a discrepancy from this plan.

# Objectives {#sec-objectives}

The studies of this plan have the following objectives.

(i) To estimate the offsets of a bench-scale tangential flow filtration (TFF) model of the commercial skid from manufacturing scale, as the basis of its qualification (PCMP-001 §7.1).
(ii) To determine the effect of the number of diavolumes, the transmembrane pressure (TMP) and the final DS concentration on aggregate and on the acidic charge variants of the drug substance, over the ranges given in @sec-factors.
(iii) To establish the number of diavolumes at which the retentate reaches the formulation buffer, so that the lower edge of the operating range rests on data for A-Mab and not on platform practice alone.
(iv) To establish a PAR for each of the `{python} w(n_par)` parameters against the criteria of @sec-crit-pq, by the analysis of @sec-par.
(v) To provide the evidence on which the `{python} w(n_par)` parameters will be classified under SOP-4001, and to carry that classification into the control strategy through PCR-010 and PCMR-001.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge {#sec-uo}

The UF/DF step concentrates the antibody and exchanges the process buffer for the formulation buffer. Both operations run across a tangential flow membrane whose pores pass buffer salts and retain the antibody. Ultrafiltration removes permeate and raises the antibody concentration in the retentate. Diafiltration then adds formulation buffer at the rate at which permeate leaves, so the retentate volume stays constant while the permeable species are washed out. Each diavolume removes a fixed fraction of the permeable species that remain. The residual process buffer components therefore fall exponentially with the number of diavolumes, and the number is set so that the retentate reaches the composition of the formulation buffer (@sec-crit-pq). The step ends with a second concentration to the DS target of `{python} g(sp(pconc))` g/L and a buffer flush that recovers the retentate.

The step can add to aggregate and to the acidic charge variants. The first route is mechanical. The membrane retains the antibody, so the antibody accumulates at the membrane wall in a polarization layer, where its concentration is higher than in the bulk retentate. The whole retentate also passes many times through the recirculation pump. Aggregate can form in both places, because there the antibody is most concentrated and most sheared.

The A-Mab case study leaves the UF/DF step out [@amab2009, p. 86], so it gives no expectation for this step. The expectations in the rest of this section come from general knowledge of the tangential flow filtration of antibodies. On that basis the risk of aggregate formation is expected to rise with the final concentration, with the TMP and with the number of passes through the pump. The TMP drives the permeate flux. Beyond the point at which the polarization layer limits the flux, a higher TMP compresses that layer without raising throughput, and it raises the antibody concentration at the wall. The shear at the wall is set by the crossflow and by the geometry of the feed channel. The final concentration sets the viscosity of the retentate and the concentration in the polarization layer. A higher viscosity raises the pressure drop along the feed channel and the shear stress near the end of the concentration. Within the normal operating ranges (NORs) the antibody spends little time at the highest wall concentration and passes through the pump a limited number of times. The effect on aggregate is therefore expected to be small.

The second route is chemical. The step keeps the antibody in solution for the length of the operation, and deamidation of asparagine residues continues during that time. Deamidation raises the acidic charge variants. The increase grows with the time in solution, at a rate that rises with pH and temperature. The number of diavolumes and the TMP set how long the operation lasts, the first through the volume of buffer exchanged and the second through the flux. For this reason the final retentate of every run is assayed for charge variants as well as for aggregate.

The step is part of the platform train that was used for X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab (PCMP-001 §2). Where and why aggregate forms in the step does not depend on the antibody, so that experience applies to the qualitative behaviour of the step. How readily an antibody aggregates does depend on the antibody, and so does the viscosity of its retentate, which rises steeply as the concentration approaches the DS target. For this reason the final DS concentration is studied for A-Mab and is not carried over from the platform.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqa}

The studies measure `{python} w(len(CQA_DF))` attributes of the drug substance across the step. @tbl-cqa lists them with their drug substance criteria, the method that measures each in these studies, and the criticality assigned in the A-Mab attribute assessment [@amab2009; @ichq9].

```{python}
#| output: asis
_crit_word = {"VL": "very low", "L": "low", "M": "moderate", "H": "high", "VH": "very high"}
_cqa_tbl = pd.DataFrame({
    "Attribute": list(CQA_DF["CQA"]),
    "Criterion": [AGG_CRIT + " HMW", AV_CRIT],
    "Method": [f"SEC, {AMV_SEC}", f"icIEF, {AMV_ICIEF}"],
    "Criticality": list(CQA_DF["Criticality"]),
    "Tool #1 score": list(CQA_DF["Tool #1"]),
})
_codes = list(dict.fromkeys(CQA_DF["Criticality"]))
T.frame(_cqa_tbl, "Quality attributes measured across the step, with their drug substance criteria.",
        "tbl-cqa", align=["P{4.4cm}", "l", "l", "l", "r"],
        notes=[("", " ".join(f"{c}, {_crit_word[c]} criticality." for c in _codes)
                + " Tool #1 score, the impact of the attribute on safety and efficacy multiplied by the"
                " uncertainty of that impact (A-Mab attribute assessment).")]).show()
```

Aggregate is the attribute most at risk at this step, from pump shear and from the high antibody concentration at the membrane wall. The acidic charge variants are measured because deamidation continues while the antibody is in solution on the skid. Both attributes arrive with the load. They arise in the production bioreactor, and aggregate is reduced at the cation exchange step. The studies measure what this step adds to each, against the load from the virus filtration step.

The other attributes of the register are not measured across the step. Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose arise in the production bioreactor, and no downstream step changes them (PCMP-001 §3). The membrane retains every glycoform of the antibody, so the step cannot change their distribution. Host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A are cleared by the chromatography steps before this one. PCMP-001 Table 7.1 credits this step with no clearance of host cell protein or leached Protein A, and residual DNA is judged on the drug substance only (PCMP-001 §7.3).

Fragments are not measured either. They form by proteolytic clipping of the antibody, in culture and during the harvest hold (PCMP-001 §3), and by non-enzymatic hydrolysis of the hinge region, which proceeds slowly with time in solution. The step adds no protease, and pump shear and the concentration at the wall aggregate the antibody without cleaving it. Hinge hydrolysis continues on the skid, but over the duration of the operation it is expected to add little. Version 1.0 left fragments out of the studies of this step, and this amendment keeps that scope. PCMP-001 assumes that this step does not change fragments (PCMP-001 Table 7.1), and the drug substance is tested for fragments at release.

Viral clearance is credited to the `{python} CLAIMS_TXT` steps, and the cumulative claim is consolidated in PCMR-001 [@ichq5a]. It is not measured at this step.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters {#sec-risk}

RA-001 ranked every process parameter of the drug substance process for its potential impact on the CQAs and on process performance, and for its potential to interact with other parameters [@ichq9]. Parameters ranked high, or with a likely interaction, were assigned to multivariate study. Parameters ranked lower, whose range could be supported one factor at a time, were assigned to univariate study (PCMP-001 §4). All `{python} w(n_par)` parameters of this step were assigned to univariate study.

The `{python} w(n_par)` parameters act on the product by different routes. More diavolumes wash more of the permeable process buffer components out of the retentate, and they add time on the skid and passes through the pump. A higher TMP raises the permeate flux until the polarization layer limits it. Beyond that point it raises the antibody concentration at the membrane wall without raising throughput. A higher final DS concentration raises the bulk concentration of the retentate, and with it the viscosity, the pressure drop along the feed channel and the concentration at the membrane wall.

The TMP and the final DS concentration both raise the antibody concentration at the membrane wall. The TMP does so by driving more permeate through the polarization layer, and the final DS concentration by raising the bulk concentration that feeds the layer. An interaction between them is therefore possible. A study that varies one factor at a time cannot resolve such an interaction. What the design does bound is the effect of each parameter at the edge of its range studied, with the other parameters at the values the commercial step will hold. Version 1.0 set a rule for this case, and this plan keeps it. Where a measured attribute approaches its acceptance criterion at an edge, the study should be extended to the combination of edges before a range is claimed, and the extension should be agreed with Statistics and QA before it is executed. Version 1.0 set no threshold for an attribute that approaches its criterion, and PCR-010 states how the rule was applied.

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The studies are run on the bench-scale skid `{python} TFF`, registered as the `{python} TFF_DESC` and held under calibration and change control. @sec-schedule gives its calibration status for each study. The model holds the crossflow and the membrane loading at their commercial values, both scaled by membrane area (PCMP-001 §5). The crossflow per unit membrane area sets the shear at the membrane wall, and it sweeps retained antibody back into the bulk, so it also sets the antibody concentration in the polarization layer. The membrane loading, in grams of antibody per square metre, sets the volume that each square metre of membrane processes. At the same TMP and crossflow the flux is the same, so a run of the model lasts as long as the commercial step at the same settings. The membrane chemistry, the nominal molecular weight cut-off and the feed channel geometry are those of the commercial skid. The TMP, the number of diavolumes and the final concentration do not depend on scale and are set at the values under study.

One quantity cannot be matched. The ratio of pump displacement to system hold-up volume is larger at bench scale, so the antibody passes through the pump more often per gram processed than at commercial scale. The bench model is therefore expected to be conservative for aggregate formation by shear.

The qualification runs are made under SOP-1001, in study `{python} SDM_ST.id`, where `{python} w(N_SDM)` runs at the set-point condition are compared with the pilot and commercial record of the step on the step yield, the permeate flux at the set-point TMP, the final concentration achieved and the change in aggregate content across the step. PCMP-001 §5 lists the same outputs for this step. Version 1.0 did not state which batches of that record form the reference, and PCR-010 states which do. Under PCMP-001 §7.1 the offset of each output is the mean of the scale-down runs at set-point minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches, reported with its two-sided `{python} CI` % confidence interval. Each end of that interval is a one-sided `{python} CI_SIDE` % confidence bound. PCMP-001 requires the qualification runs, and the estimate of each offset, before the first characterization run of a step.

@tbl-sdm-outputs shows how each output of the qualification is used. Of the outputs that the qualification compares, only aggregate carries a criterion at this step, the drug substance criterion for aggregate in the final retentate (@sec-crit-pq). Every judgement of a scale-down aggregate result against that criterion first subtracts the aggregate offset, as PCMP-001 §7.1 requires for an output with a criterion, so the conclusion is stated at manufacturing scale. PCR-010 states how the offset of the change across the step applies to the level in the final retentate. The step yield, the permeate flux and the final concentration have no criterion at the step, and their offsets are recorded only.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_sdm_out = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Step yield", "Yes", "None", "Recorded only"],
    [f"Permeate flux at the set-point TMP of {g(sp(ptmp))} psi", "Yes", "None", "Recorded only"],
    ["Final concentration achieved", "Yes", "None", "Recorded only"],
    ["Change in aggregate content across the step", "Yes", f"{AGG_CRIT} HMW in the final retentate",
     "Subtracted before every judgement"],
    ["Acidic charge variants", "No", f"{AV_CRIT} in the final retentate", "None, the offset is unknown"],
    ["Buffer exchange (conductivity and pH)", "No",
     f"Plateau of the formulation buffer at or below {g(nor(pdv)[0])} DV", "None, the offset is unknown"],
], columns=["Output", "Compared at\nboth scales", "Criterion at the step", "Use of the offset"])
T.frame(_sdm_out, "Outputs of the scale-down qualification and the use of their offsets.",
        "tbl-sdm-outputs", align=["P{4.4cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "P{4.2cm}", "P{3.6cm}"]).show()
```

The acidic charge variants and the buffer exchange also carry criteria at this step, but the qualification does not compare them at both scales. Their offsets are therefore unknown, not zero (PCMP-001 §7.1). Each is judged as the scale-down model measures it. For the acidic charge variants this rests on the kinetics of deamidation, which depend on the pH and the temperature of the solution and on the time spent in it, and not on the scale of the skid. The model runs under the operation procedure of the commercial step (SOP-2013) in the commercial formulation buffer, and a run lasts as long as the commercial step at the same settings. For the buffer exchange it rests on the passage of the buffer species through the membrane, which depends on the number of diavolumes and on the membrane and not on scale.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

The step receives the filtrate pool of the small virus retentive filtration step. The pool is concentrated by ultrafiltration, diafiltered at constant volume against formulation buffer for the planned number of diavolumes, concentrated a second time to the final target, and recovered with a buffer flush. Operation follows SOP-2013. At the set-point condition the step runs `{python} g(sp(pdv))` DV at a TMP of `{python} g(sp(ptmp))` psi to a final concentration of `{python} g(sp(pconc))` g/L.

All runs of the study are loaded from a single pool of the virus filtration step, so that the variability of the load does not confound the comparison between the levels of a parameter. @sec-risks gives the bridging rule that applies if one pool is not sufficient.

## Analytical methods {#sec-analytical}

The validated methods are listed in @tbl-sops. Aggregate is measured by size exclusion chromatography (SEC) under `{python} AMV_SEC` and reported as the percentage of high molecular weight species (HMW). Protein concentration is measured by ultraviolet absorbance (A280) under AMV-3019. The mass balance and the final concentration rest on that measurement. Charge variants are measured by imaged capillary isoelectric focusing (icIEF) under `{python} AMV_ICIEF` and reported as the percentage of acidic species. The completeness of the buffer exchange is followed by the conductivity and the pH of the retentate. These are in-process measurements read from the skid instrumentation and are not validated assays, so they are used to characterize the exchange curve and not to release a run.

This step has no designed experiment. Its univariate studies measure aggregate by SEC, which PCMP-001 §7.8 keeps as the method for aggregate, and they do not measure fragments, which Version 1.0 left out of their scope (@sec-cqa).

Aggregate in the load of this step is expected to be low. Aggregate binds the cation exchange resin more strongly than the monomer, so it elutes late and is largely excluded from the pool at the cation exchange step. A change across this step may therefore be of the same size as the repeatability of the SEC method. Version 1.0 set the following rule for this case, and it is unchanged. Analytical Development will report the method variability that applies over the range in which the samples fall. A measured change is judged against the pure error estimate described in @sec-stats rather than against the nominal precision of the method.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

Samples are taken at the points listed in @tbl-sampling. The acceptance criteria of @sec-crit-pq apply to the final retentate. The other samples support the mass balance, the buffer exchange curve and the confirmation that the membrane retains the antibody.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_sampling = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Load pool", "Virus filtration filtrate, before ultrafiltration", "A280, SEC, icIEF",
     "Fixes the input to every run in the study"],
    ["Pre-diafiltration retentate", "End of the first concentration", "A280",
     "Confirms the concentration at which diafiltration starts"],
    ["Diafiltration series", "After each diavolume", "Conductivity, pH^a)^",
     "Builds the buffer exchange curve"],
    ["Final retentate", "After the final concentration and recovery flush", "A280, SEC, icIEF",
     "The drug substance sample the acceptance criteria apply to"],
    ["Permeate", "Composite over the run", "A280", "Confirms that the membrane retains the antibody"],
], columns=["Sample", "Point in the step", "Tests", "Purpose"])
T.frame(_sampling, "Sampling plan for each characterization run.", "tbl-sampling",
        align=["P{3.2cm}", "P{4.4cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "P{4.6cm}"],
        notes=[("a)", "Read from the skid instrumentation. In-process measurements, not validated assays.")]
        ).show()
```

Every sample will be assayed within the stability period established for the matrix, and the load pool sample will be assayed once for the whole study rather than once per run. Where a run is repeated, the repeat carries its own sample set.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

For each parameter and each response, the measured values will be regressed on the level of the parameter over the range studied, and the slope will be tested against zero at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`. The set-point condition is shared by the `{python} w(n_par)` series and will be run `{python} w(n_sp)` times. Those replicates give the pure error estimate of the combined process and assay variability, against which a change across a range is read. PCMP-001 §6.2 sets the same level for the significance of a model term, and under it an attribute is called affected by a parameter when the slope is significant at that level.

Statistical significance and practical significance will be reported separately. A slope that is significant at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)` but predicts a change across the range that is small against the acceptance criterion will be described in those terms, and the criterion rather than the p-value decides whether the range is acceptable. No response-surface model will be fitted for this step, because the design carries no factorial structure and no interaction term can be estimated from it. The `{python} w(n_lev)` levels of each series, with the set-point replicated, do allow a curvature to be detected for that parameter on its own. The model-adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 apply to response-surface models and therefore do not apply here.

The buffer exchange will be analysed separately. The conductivity of the retentate will be plotted against the number of diavolumes, and the exponential decay expected from @sec-uo will be fitted to the series. The analysis reports the number of diavolumes at which the conductivity of the retentate has reached the plateau set by the formulation buffer and no further change is measured over the following diavolume.

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and study type {#sec-factors}

The parameters, their set-points, the ranges to be studied and the NORs are given in @tbl-params. All `{python} w(n_par)` are studied one at a time, because RA-001 ranked none of them high and judged that their ranges could be supported one factor at a time (@sec-risk).

```{python}
#| output: asis
_pp = plan_params(UO).drop(columns=["Study type"])
_pp["Set-point"] = _pp["Set-point"].map(g)
T.frame(_pp,
        "Parameters, ranges studied and normal operating ranges for the step.", "tbl-params",
        align=["P{5.0cm}", "l", "r", "l", "l"]).show()
```

Each range studied extends beyond the NOR at one end or at both. The number of diavolumes is studied from `{python} g(prg(pdv)[0])` to `{python} g(prg(pdv)[1])` DV against a NOR of `{python} g(nor(pdv)[0])` to `{python} g(nor(pdv)[1])` DV. The range extends above the NOR because more diavolumes mean more time on the skid and more passes through the pump. Its lower edge is the lower edge of the NOR, which is the lowest count the commercial step will run, and the buffer exchange curve characterizes the step at that value. Below that edge the buffer exchange would be less complete, and the study does not go there. The TMP is studied from `{python} g(prg(ptmp)[0])` to `{python} g(prg(ptmp)[1])` psi against a NOR of `{python} g(nor(ptmp)[0])` to `{python} g(nor(ptmp)[1])` psi. The range extends above the NOR because a higher TMP raises the antibody concentration at the membrane wall. Its lower edge is also the lower edge of the NOR. A lower TMP would lengthen the operation, and with it the passes through the pump and the time for deamidation, and the study does not characterize that side beyond the NOR.

The final DS concentration is studied from `{python} g(prg(pconc)[0])` to `{python} g(prg(pconc)[1])` g/L against a NOR of `{python} g(nor(pconc)[0])` to `{python} g(nor(pconc)[1])` g/L, and the range extends on both sides. An excursion above the target raises the viscosity of the retentate and the antibody concentration at the wall, and with them the risk of aggregation. An excursion below the target leaves the drug substance below the concentration that the drug product program expects.

The step will not be characterized outside these ranges, and no range wider than the range studied will be proposed in PCR-010.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

Each parameter is run at `{python} w(n_lev)` levels, the two edges of its range studied and its set-point, with the other `{python} w(n_par - 1)` parameters held at their set-points. The set-point condition is common to the `{python} w(n_par)` series, so the study consists of `{python} w(n_edge)` edge runs and `{python} w(n_sp)` replicates of the set-point condition, `{python} w(n_runs)` runs in all. The planned runs are listed in Appendix A (@tbl-levels).

The order of execution is randomized across the whole study, subject to the constraint that all runs draw from the load pool of @sec-operation. Each run is sampled as described in @sec-sampling, and its final retentate is assayed by SEC, A280 and icIEF. The diavolume series carries the additional in-process sampling that builds the buffer exchange curve.

# Acceptance and decision criteria {#sec-criteria}

PCMP-001 §7 sets the framework of acceptance criteria that every step plan applies. This section states the criteria of that framework for the outputs of this step, and the rules of Version 1.0 by which the studies are decided.

## Scale-down model {#sec-crit-sdm}

Version 1.0 accepted the model under a rule in three parts. The mean step yield, the permeate flux and the change in aggregate content across the step were not to differ from the pilot and commercial record at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`. The final concentration achieved was to lie within the reported variability of the A280 method. A difference that was statistically significant was to be assessed for its size against the acceptance criteria of @sec-crit-pq before the model was rejected, and that judgement was to be documented in the qualification record and approved by Statistics and QA.

PCMP-001 Version 2.0 replaces such tests with the offset for every scale-down model (PCMP-001 §7.1). The offset is subtracted from each aggregate result and recorded for the other outputs that the qualification compares (@sec-sdm). Under PCMP-001 a model is qualified for an output when the conclusion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its confidence interval, and that conclusion is drawn from the response-surface model of the step. This step has no response-surface model, so the decision cannot be made as PCMP-001 states it, and this plan has no rule for it. PCR-010 states the approach it takes.

## Product quality {#sec-crit-pq}

The final retentate is judged against the drug substance criteria of @tbl-cqa. Aggregate must not exceed `{python} g(ACC_AGG[1])` % HMW, and the acidic charge variants must lie between `{python} g(ACC_AV[0])` and `{python} g(ACC_AV[1])` %. PCMP-001 §7.3 carries each drug substance criterion back through the platform worst cases of the downstream steps to give the IACs of the steps before this one. No step follows this one, so there is nothing to carry a criterion back through, and PCMP-001 Table 7.1 defines no IAC for this step. The drug substance criteria therefore apply directly (PCMP-001 §7.6). They come from the drug substance CQA register (PCMP-001 §3), and no result of the studies of this plan enters them.

Each run is judged on its own measured result, which is a single batch, as PCMP-001 §6.2 requires for a quality attribute. The offset of the acidic charge variants is unknown, because the qualification does not compare them, and each result is judged as measured (PCMP-001 §7.1).

The derivation in PCMP-001 assumes that no step after `{python} LAST_AGG` changes aggregate, and that no step after `{python} LAST_AV` changes the acidic charge variants (PCMP-001 Table 7.1). This step can add to both, and the studies of this plan measure what it adds. The verification of platform worst cases in PCMP-001 §7.5 uses the response-surface model of a step, and no verification is planned at this step.

Version 1.0 set the criterion for the buffer exchange, and it is unchanged. The buffer exchange is accepted when the conductivity and the pH of the retentate have reached the plateau of the formulation buffer, by the analysis of @sec-stats, at or below the lower edge of the diavolume NOR of `{python} g(nor(pdv)[0])` DV. Version 1.0 set no numerical tolerance for the plateau, and PCR-010 states the one it uses.

## Decision rules {#sec-rules}

Version 1.0 set the following decision rules, and they are unchanged.

1. A level of a parameter is acceptable when every attribute measured on the final retentate of that run meets its criterion.
2. A parameter passes over its range studied when every level in the range is acceptable and the change measured across the range is small against the criterion.
3. Where a level fails, the range is truncated at the last acceptable level, and the failing level is reported as an edge of failure.
4. Where a failure occurs at a level inside the NOR, execution stops, and the operating range is reviewed with the receiving site and with QA before the study continues.
5. Where a run fails for a reason attributable to the equipment or to the method, and not to the parameter under study, the run may be repeated once. Both the original and the repeat are reported in PCR-010.

Version 1.0 set no threshold for a change that is small against the criterion, and PCMP-001 sets none. PCR-010 states how it judges such a change.

## Classification {#sec-class}

Each parameter will be classified under SOP-4001 [@ichq8; @ichq11]. Version 1.0 set the following rule, and this plan keeps it. A parameter whose variation over the characterized range affects no quality attribute, but whose control is needed for the step to perform consistently, is classified as a key process parameter. A parameter whose variation affects a quality attribute is classified as critical, or as well controlled critical where the risk of falling outside the design space is low. The classification is an outcome of the studies and is reported in PCR-010.

PCMP-001 Version 2.0 adds the following to that rule (PCMP-001 §6.2, §7.7). Whether a parameter affects an attribute is decided by the slope test of @sec-stats. A significant effect that is too small to move the attribute appreciably within the PAR does not by itself make a parameter critical. A parameter is well-controlled critical when its risk of falling outside its acceptable range is low, because it is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR. A parameter studied one factor at a time is classified by the same rules as a parameter studied in a design (PCMP-001 §4). PCMP-001 and SOP-4001 set no numerical threshold for a small effect or a wide PAR. PCR-010 will therefore state the size of each effect across the PAR and the margin of the PAR to the NOR, and classify on them.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis) {#sec-par}

A PAR will be assigned to each parameter from its univariate series. The acceptance basis is the drug substance criteria of @tbl-cqa, because PCMP-001 defines no IAC for this step. The PAR of a parameter is the contiguous span of levels over which every attribute measured on the final retentate met its criterion, with the other parameters at their set-points. Each PAR will be reported in PCR-010 together with the measured series and the criterion against which it was read.

Three bounds apply to a PAR determined this way, and PCR-010 will state them where it states the ranges.

1. A univariate PAR holds with the other parameters at their set-points. It does not describe the step when two parameters sit at their range edges at the same time.
2. PCMP-001 §6.4 defines a second analysis, the NOR-propagated analysis. It predicts the response from a fitted multivariate model while each other parameter is drawn at random from a normal distribution around its set-point, with a standard deviation of the width of its NOR divided by `{python} g(NOR_DIV)`, clipped to the range studied. This step has no such model, so the NOR-propagated analysis is not performed. PCMP-001 §7.6 defines a PAR through that analysis, and for a parameter studied one factor at a time the range rests on its own data instead (PCMP-001 §4).
3. A PAR cannot be wider than the range studied. Where every level in a range is acceptable, the claimed PAR is the range studied of @tbl-params and nothing beyond it, and it is reported as reaching the edge of that range (PCMP-001 §7.6).

The ranges reported under this analysis become the basis of the operating ranges that the receiving site runs to, together with the classification of @sec-class. Where a PAR is wider than the NOR, the margin between them is what a deviation is dispositioned against. Where a PAR is truncated at an edge of failure, the NOR should be reviewed against the truncated range before the step is transferred.

# Data management and integrity {#sec-data}

Data generated under this plan are recorded so that they are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate, and so that they remain complete, consistent, enduring and available (ALCOA+). Run records are captured in the electronic notebook under the study number. Analytical results are captured in the laboratory information management system and reported against the sample identifiers of @tbl-sampling. The study record also gives the execution window of each study and the calibration status of the equipment it used. INV-001 preventive action PA3 requires the execution dates and the calibration status of the equipment in every study record.

The statistical analysis of @sec-stats is scripted and held under version control, so that it can be re-executed on the retained raw data and return the same result. Every calculation is reviewed by a second qualified person. A change to a record after it has been made carries an audit trail with the reason for the change. Values quoted in PCR-010 are read from the retained data set and are not re-entered by hand. Records are retained under the record retention procedure of the sponsor for the life of the product.

# Deliverables and schedule {#sec-schedule}

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-010, the process characterization report for the step. PCR-010 reports the qualification of the scale-down model, the `{python} w(n_par)` univariate series, the buffer exchange curve, the PARs and the parameter classification, and it rolls up into PCMR-001.

The work runs in the following order.

1. The qualification runs of the scale-down model, which PCMP-001 §7.1 requires before the first characterization run, together with the estimate of each offset.
2. The characterization runs of @sec-univariate, from a single load pool.
3. The analysis of @sec-stats and the PAR determination of @sec-par, after the last run.
4. The drafting, review and approval of PCR-010.
5. The transfer of the classification and the ranges into the control strategy and into PCMR-001.

Version 1.0 gave no calendar dates. The studies of this plan ran in the windows of @tbl-windows, on the skid `{python} TFF`, whose next calibration was due on `{python} TFF_DUE`. A window runs from the first to the last day of execution in the study record. The qualification study ended before the univariate study began, so the two studies did not run in parallel. Both windows closed before the calibration due date, and the skid was in calibration at execution. The campaign schedule is held in PCMP-001 and the transfer milestones in PTP-001.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_kind = {"qualification": "Scale-down model qualification", "univariate": "Univariate"}
_win = pd.DataFrame([[r.id, _kind[r.kind], r.start, r.end] for r in plan_st.itertuples()],
                    columns=["Study", "Study type", "Start", "End"])
T.frame(_win, "Execution windows of the studies of this plan.", "tbl-windows",
        align=["l", "P{5.0cm}", "l", "l"]).show()
```

# Risks and assumptions {#sec-risks}

The scale-down model gives more passes through the pump per gram of antibody than the commercial skid (@sec-sdm). The model is therefore expected to be conservative for aggregate formation, and a result that meets the criterion at bench scale is expected to hold at commercial scale. Version 1.0 set the following rule for a failure at bench scale, and it is unchanged. If aggregate fails its criterion at bench scale, the condition will be repeated at pilot scale before an operating range is narrowed on the strength of the bench result.

The study depends on a single pool of the virus filtration step for its load. If one pool is not sufficient for the whole study, a second pool will be bridged by running the set-point condition on both pools and comparing the responses against the pure error estimate of @sec-stats. A difference larger than the pure error will be investigated before the second pool is used, and the runs executed on each pool will be identified in PCR-010.

The change in aggregate across the step may be small against the variability of the SEC method. Version 1.0 set the following rule for that case, and it is unchanged. Noise near the low end of the method range will be attributed to the assay rather than to the parameter under study, unless the change measured across the range is larger than the pure error estimate of @sec-stats. Version 1.0 did not say how this rule relates to the slope test of @sec-stats, and PCR-010 states how it applies the two together.

The design has one run at each edge of a range. The slope test of each series therefore rests on few runs, and an effect that is small against the variability between runs may not reach significance.

The plan rests on the following assumptions.

1. The composition of the formulation buffer is fixed by the drug product program. A change to the formulation would change the target of the buffer exchange and would invalidate the diavolume study.
2. The membrane chemistry and the membrane supplier are as qualified, and a change to either requires a new risk assessment before these data are applied.
3. The material entering the step arrives within the criteria that PCMP-001 sets for the output of the virus filtration step (PCMP-001 Table 7.1). The study characterizes the step under representative load, and it does not challenge the step with material that is already outside those criteria.

# Approvals {#sec-approvals}

This plan takes effect when it has been approved by the functions recorded in the Approvals table at the front of this document. A change to the design, to the ranges or to the acceptance criteria after approval requires a revision of this plan, approved by the same functions, before the affected runs are executed. A departure from the plan during execution will be recorded as a deviation, dispositioned by QA, and reported with its impact assessment in PCR-010. Work that the plan did not foresee, and that departs from no approved procedure, is recorded in PCR-010 as a discrepancy from this plan.
